title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: TERRY'S BUS
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Terry Lund, a bus driver in Tacoma, Washington.
Twenty-six years behind the wheel. Then the city gave him a new boss. She was twenty-seven.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE NEW BOSS
segments.quote: Progress is impossible without change; and those who cannot change their minds, cannot change anything.
segments.author: George Bernard Shaw
lines: Jasmine Cole showed up with a tablet and fourteen new ideas.
Terry grumbled. We tried that in nineteen ninety-nine.
His buddy Ray, a mechanic, had a line from the Irish writer George Bernard Shaw taped to his toolbox:
Progress is impossible without change; and those who cannot change their minds, cannot change anything.
Terry put down his coffee and went to hear idea number one.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE ROADEO
segments.quote: Personally I am always ready to learn, although I do not always like being taught.
segments.author: Winston Churchill
lines: Idea number one was the regional Bus Roadeo. Yes, a rodeo for buses.
Cones, and tennis balls your tires must touch without squishing.
Jasmine signed him up and started giving him tips. Terry's ears turned red.
His wife Linda smiled and quoted Winston Churchill:
Personally I am always ready to learn, although I do not always like being taught.
Terry laughed. Okay. Teach me, boss.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: ONE TRICK A DAY
segments.quote: Nothing is particularly hard if you divide it into small jobs.
segments.author: Henry Ford
lines: Terry missed all eleven tricks the first night.
Jasmine showed him a line from Henry Ford:
Nothing is particularly hard if you divide it into small jobs.
So every evening he practiced one trick. Just one.
Monday, the tight turn. Tuesday, backing up. By Friday, the cones were safe.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE FLAT CONE
segments.quote: Experience is not what happens to a man; it is what a man does with what happens to him.
segments.author: Aldous Huxley
lines: Then came a practice run in front of the whole garage.
Terry flattened a cone like a pancake. The mechanics gave him a standing ovation.
He wanted to quit. Ray handed him a note from the English writer Aldous Huxley:
Experience is not what happens to a man; it is what a man does with what happens to him.
Terry stood the cone back up and backed in clean. Three times.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: TWO TEACHERS
segments.quote: We are all apprentices in a craft where no one ever becomes a master.
segments.author: Ernest Hemingway
lines: One night, Jasmine tried the driver's seat herself, and she was scared.
Terry knew just what to say. Hands low. Eyes far. Breathe.
Her tablet made him sharper. His hands made her braver.
She stuck a note from Ernest Hemingway over the windshield:
We are all apprentices in a craft where no one ever becomes a master.
Both students. Both teachers.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE RAIN
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: Roadeo day, it poured. Of course. This is Tacoma.
Other drivers raced the clock and sent cones flying like bowling pins.
Terry remembered his grandpa's favorite line from Ben Franklin:
Haste makes waste.
So he drove slow and smooth. Every tennis ball touched. Not one squished.
He took first place. Jasmine cried louder than his wife.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Change your mind. Be teachable. Small steps. Get up. Teach each other. Slow down.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Change your mind. Be teachable. Take small steps. Get up. Teach each other. Slow down.
Me? I tried to park a golf cart once. The golf cart won.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
